article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Eye Candy × Jokerz #31
Breeder: Compound Genetics
THC Content: 24-27%
CBD Content: Typically low
Terpene Profile: limonene , beta-caryophyllene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Fuel, earthy mint, sweet candy, herbs
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September / early October
Indoor Yield: High
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Candy Bezels approaches modern cannabis from two directions at once. One side is unmistakably old-school: fuel, damp earth, kush-like herbs, and a cooling mint quality that can recall the sharper gas strains of an earlier generation. The other side is thoroughly contemporary, adding candy sweetness, floral cream, dark purple flowers, and the dense trichome coverage now associated with elite boutique marijuana. Compound Genetics created that contrast by crossing Eye Candy with Jokerz #31, two parents already recognized for exceptional resin production and visually impressive flower. Rather than producing a completely uniform seed line, the cross offers several worthwhile directions for phenotype hunting, with some plants leaning toward earthy mint and others expressing sweeter Runtz-like candy gas.

The strain is not merely attractive in a jar. Compound Genetics selected the combination around high yield, fast finishing, and flower quality that remains strong even when production is pushed. Most phenotypes complete bloom in about eight weeks, while slower individuals may need a ninth. Tight calyx formation, dark coloration, soft orange pistils, and a heavy frost of resin give mature buds considerable bag appeal, while the underlying aroma remains assertive enough to keep the cultivar from becoming another visually impressive but indistinct sweet hybrid.
Genetics and Lineage

Candy Bezels is a direct cross of Eye Candy × Jokerz #31. Eye Candy was created by Compound Genetics from Biscotti × The Menthol , bringing together two lines with very different but complementary aromatic qualities. Biscotti contributes dense Cookies-family flower , sweetness, spice, and a creamy dessert background, while The Menthol adds aggressive fuel, herbal sharpness, and the cooling mint character that gives Eye Candy its recognizable identity. Compound Genetics describes Eye Candy as a gas-dominant cultivar with only a light layer of sweetness in the aroma, although that sweetness becomes more apparent in the smoke.

Jokerz #31 supplies the modern candy-gas half of the pedigree. Compound Genetics created Jokerz from White Runtz × Jet Fuel Gelato and selected phenotype #31 from a large population after evaluating plant structure, trichome development, coloration, aroma, and finished smoke quality. The keeper became notable for purple flowers, exceptional resin density, and a terpene profile built around perfume, candy, floral Gelato notes, and gas. It also commonly produces very strong cannabinoid results, which helped establish Jokerz #31 as an important breeding parent throughout Compound’s later collections.

Combining those lines gives Candy Bezels several overlapping sources of gas while allowing individual phenotypes to move in different sensory directions. Eye Candy can dominate with earth, herbs, mint, and kushy fuel, while Jokerz #31 may push the flower toward sweeter candy, cream, perfume, and Runtz-like characteristics. Compound Genetics observed substantial variation during its phenotype hunt, yet nearly all selections retained some degree of gas. That shared fuel backbone is what holds the genetic range together and gives the cultivar a consistent identity even when individual plants smell noticeably different.
Effects and Experience

The experience usually begins with a quick change in mood rather than an immediate physical shutdown. A moderate serving can create a brighter, more amused headspace accompanied by an easy sense of euphoria. Conversation may become more engaging, music can feel more immersive, and routine entertainment often takes on a lighter tone. There is enough cerebral activity to keep the beginning of the experience interesting, but the effect does not generally have the sharp, restless quality associated with intensely stimulating sativas.

Physical relaxation becomes more obvious as the session develops. Shoulders loosen, movement feels less urgent, and the upbeat mental tone gradually becomes softer and more contented. At moderate doses, that middle stage can work well for movies, gaming, casual social settings, or simply unwinding without becoming immediately sleepy. Heavier consumption brings considerably more weight, with the body effect beginning to dominate and concentration becoming less precise.

Potency can be substantial, particularly in well-grown selections carrying strong Jokerz #31 influence. Although the breeder does not assign one universal THC figure to every plant, examples of the line are frequently placed in the mid-to-upper 20% range. Consumers with limited tolerance should therefore avoid judging strength by the sweet flavor alone. Too much can turn the pleasant cerebral lift into dizziness, dry mouth, dry eyes, mental fog, or temporary anxiety before the heavier relaxing phase settles in.
Medical Benefits

Candy Bezels may interest medical cannabis consumers who prefer a transition from mental uplift into deeper physical calm rather than immediate sedation. The early euphoric stage may help make stress, irritability, or low mood feel less intrusive, while the later body effect can reduce awareness of muscular tightness or general physical discomfort. That changing balance makes the strain particularly suited to late-afternoon or evening use, when maintaining some mental engagement at first is useful but relaxation becomes increasingly desirable.

Larger doses can produce stronger appetite stimulation and a more pronounced desire to rest. For some medical marijuana consumers, that heavier phase may fit nighttime routines better than daytime responsibilities. High potency also means that the same amount can produce very different results depending on tolerance. Someone accustomed to strong weed may find the cultivar comfortably calming, while a less experienced consumer could experience impaired concentration or an unpleasantly intense mental effect.

No single terpene panel should be treated as universal for the strain because the seed line contains meaningful phenotype variation. Limonene, beta-caryophyllene, and myrcene frequently appear in related chemistry, but actual ratios can shift substantially between plants and cultivation environments. Consumers using cannabis for medical purposes should rely on laboratory results from the specific batch whenever available and consider medications, cannabinoid strength, personal THC sensitivity, and dosage rather than assuming every Candy Bezels harvest will produce the same therapeutic experience.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Fuel forms the center of the bouquet. It can smell like gasoline, kushy resin, or sharp old-school indoor cannabis, depending on which side of the pedigree dominates. Around that base sits an earthy herbal layer inherited largely from Eye Candy and The Menthol. On some plants, the herbal quality becomes distinctly cooling, creating an earthy mint impression that separates the cultivar from more predictable candy-gas crosses.

Other phenotypes move in the opposite direction. Jokerz #31 can introduce sweeter Runtz-like candy, soft floral perfume, and a creamy quality that rounds out the sharper fuel. Compound Genetics found both expressions during selection, along with plants that blended the two almost evenly. Dark purple flower does not necessarily predict which aroma will dominate, so growers hunting for a keeper need to evaluate the finished terpene profile rather than choosing solely on appearance.

Flavor tends to reveal more sweetness than the raw aroma suggests. Fuel and earthy herbs may hit first, followed by mint, cream, and candy through the exhale. Vaporization can highlight the softer sweet and herbal details, while combustion generally makes the gas and kushy earth more prominent. A slow dry and controlled cure are especially important because the cultivar’s appeal depends on contrast; rushed processing can flatten the delicate mint and candy notes and leave little more than generic fuel.
Growing Information

Candy Bezels is a productive cannabis strain , but it benefits from growers who understand canopy management and late-flower environmental control. Plants can develop enough vigor and stretch to fill space quickly after the flowering cycle begins, so topping and low-stress training are useful for creating a broad, even canopy. A trellis can keep productive branches separated and exposed to direct light while also providing support later, when dense flower begins adding significant weight. Interior shoots that remain shaded can be removed early so the plant directs more energy toward well-lit upper sites.

Flowering is relatively fast for a modern high-yield hybrid. Most selections finish in approximately eight weeks, while others require closer to nine. Mature buds tend to form tight calyxes and can develop deep purple coloration beneath a dense layer of trichomes. That heavy resin production makes the cultivar attractive for dry sift, rosin, and ice-water hash as well as finished flower. Because compact, resinous buds can hold moisture internally, airflow should remain strong through the final weeks and humidity should be kept under control.

Outdoor cultivation can produce large plants when the root zone, sunlight, and season are sufficient. An 8–9-week flowering cycle generally places harvest from late September into October in many Northern Hemisphere gardens, although latitude and local flowering onset determine the exact timing. Compound Genetics describes the line as capable of high yields without sacrificing flower quality, but no universal grams-per-plant figure applies. Growers selecting from seed may find the greatest value in hunting several plants and keeping the individual that best combines structure, yield, resin density, color, and the preferred balance of earthy mint versus candy gas.
FAQ
What strains make Candy Bezels?
Candy Bezels was bred by Compound Genetics from Eye Candy × Jokerz #31. Eye Candy comes from Biscotti × The Menthol, while Jokerz #31 is an elite selection from White Runtz × Jet Fuel Gelato.
Is Candy Bezels indica or sativa?

It is a hybrid that commonly shows indica-leaning characteristics in flower structure and later effects. The experience can begin with noticeable mental uplift before developing into deeper physical relaxation.
What does Candy Bezels taste like?
Fuel, earth, herbs, and mint form the old-school side of the flavor profile, while sweeter phenotypes add candy, cream, and Runtz-like notes. Most plants retain at least some noticeable gas.
How long does Candy Bezels take to flower?
Compound Genetics lists an 8–9-week flowering period. Many phenotypes finish near eight weeks, while slower selections may require the full ninth week to reach maturity.
Is Candy Bezels a high-yielding strain?

Yes. Compound Genetics specifically describes the cultivar as high yielding while maintaining strong flower quality. Good light distribution, canopy training, branch support, airflow, and environmental stability help growers take advantage of that production potential.
Final Thoughts on Candy Bezels

Candy Bezels works because its parents do not simply duplicate one another. Eye Candy introduces the harsher, earthier side of cannabis—gas, herbs, kush, and mint—while Jokerz #31 supplies sweeter candy, floral perfume, color, potency, and exceptional frost. The offspring can lean strongly toward either parent, yet fuel remains the thread connecting nearly every expression.

From a cultivation perspective, the combination of an 8–9-week bloom, strong yield potential, dense trichome development, and impressive flower appearance makes the cultivar useful beyond small connoisseur gardens. It can produce commercially attractive weed without requiring an unusually long flowering schedule, while phenotype hunters still have enough variation to uncover genuinely different keeper plants.

The most memorable examples are the ones that preserve contrast rather than collapsing into generic sweetness. Earthy mint against candy, kushy herbs against cream, and old-school fuel against purple modern flower give Candy Bezels an identity that is easy to recognize. For consumers and growers drawn to contemporary Compound Genetics strains but unwilling to give up the deeper gas character of older marijuana, this hybrid offers a particularly effective bridge between the two styles.
